what: A per-sentence review of what the decomposition did with each real sentence in data/evaluation/decomposition_coverage.json.
why: Coverage is mechanical and says only whether three elements were located. Whether a refusal was correct, and whether a located element is the right one, is a judgement — so it is kept here, apart from the mechanical measurement, and never folded into it.
review_method: per-sentence read of the verbatim rule text; no document was consulted, because the four source documents were not acquired
standing: This is review input, not ground truth. A human reviewer's verdict outranks it, and nothing here may be counted toward the readiness gate, which requires human acceptance.

classifications.correct: every located element is supported by the sentence
classifications.partial: located elements are supported but one is cut short of what the sentence states
classifications.contaminated: a located span includes text that is not part of that element
classifications.wrong: a located span states something the sentence does not — the most dangerous outcome
classifications.correct_refusal: no decomposition, and the sentence does not state a directed communicative act
classifications.borderline: no decomposition, and a reviewer could reasonably read the sentence either way
classifications.defect: no decomposition, but the sentence does state one and the parser should have found it

keyed_by: sha256 of the sentence, so a review is invalidated rather than silently carried over if the sentence changes
